chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Samaan, who said:
I asked him about a man who rents land that has fruit trees on it, so he said: 'If you spend something on it, there is no harm.'

And I asked him about al-muzara'ah (sharecropping): a man sows a hundred jarib of seed or less or more of food or other things, then a man comes to him and says: 'Take half of this seed from me, and half of your expenses are upon me, and share with me in it.' He said: 'There is no harm.'

I said: 'But if the one who sowed it in the land did not buy it for a price, and it is merely something he had,' he said: 'Then he should value it at what was sold for on that day, then he takes half the price and half the expenses and shares with him.'

key_terms.اَلثَّمَرَة: Fruit; specifically referring to fruit trees or produce on the land.
key_terms.اَلْبَذْر: Seed; the grain or seeds sown in the land.
key_terms.اَلْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping; an agricultural partnership where parties share the crop.
key_terms.جَرِيب: Jarib; a unit of area measurement used in classical Islamic land measurement.
key_terms.نِصْفُ نَفَقَتِكَ: Half of your expenses; the share of costs borne by one partner.
key_terms.يُقَوِّمُهُ: He values it; to assess the monetary worth of an item.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid sharecropping (muzara'ah) and land rental in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping) by addressing specific economic conditions, such as tenant-incurred expenses and the valuation of pre-owned seed capital. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in agricultural partnerships, ensuring that contributions of both labor and assets are equitably compensated. The ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic contract law in accommodating varying forms of capital contribution in agrarian societies.
